subject.title: Feature Request: Voice Recognition / Speaker Identification for Voice Interface

question: Should OpenClaw add enrolled-speaker gating for Voice Wake, push-to-talk, and Talk, and what security/storage/provider boundary should govern voice profiles and fallback behavior?
rationale: The request affects who may trigger voice actions and how biometric-like voice data is stored or sent to providers, which cannot be safely inferred from current code or a single implementation suggestion.

options.title: Design speaker-gating contract first
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define the enrollment, storage, threshold, provider-egress, fallback, and native/plugin API contract before implementation.

options.title: Limit to native local prototype
options.body: Scope an initial design to local-only macOS speaker verification and explicitly defer provider diarization and mobile support until the boundary is proven.

options.title: Defer speaker identification
options.body: Keep the existing wake-word, push-to-talk, and Talk behavior until maintainers are ready to treat speaker matching as a supported security-sensitive feature.

recommendation.title: Design speaker-gating contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define the enrollment, storage, threshold, provider-egress, fallback, and native/plugin API contract before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history across macOS voice activation, Talk, and gateway voice surfaces implicated by the decision.
